strengths: Honest and transparent reporting of a negative result, which is valuable for the community to avoid redundant work
Clear diagnostic analysis identifying candidate homogeneity as the root cause of failure, with quantitative support (90.6% identical pages at temperature 0.1)
Training-free method is well-motivated and practically appealing; the framing of traditional OCR as a proxy verifier is intuitive
The insight about best-of-N requiring diversity to be effective is a useful takeaway for future work in inference-time scaling for document tasks
weaknesses: Thin contribution: the core finding (low-temperature models produce homogeneous outputs so selection fails) is arguably predictable without running experiments, reducing the novelty of the negative result
The obvious fix—raising temperature—is not systematically explored; the paper would be stronger if it characterized the diversity-accuracy tradeoff across temperatures
Single benchmark evaluation (olmOCR-Bench) limits generalizability of conclusions; different document types or base models may behave differently
The anchor-token coverage metric is a reasonable heuristic but its failure modes beyond homogeneity are not analyzed, leaving open whether a better reranker could succeed

ai_detection.reasoning: The introduction follows a highly formulaic four-paragraph structure (problem → prior work → method → results) culminating in a mechanically enumerated 'Our contributions are:' bullet list—a classic AI writing pattern. Prose is uniformly clean and terse with no sentence-level variation, idiomatic phrasing, or narrative voice. The four bullet points mirror the preceding paragraphs nearly verbatim, a redundancy common in AI-generated academic text.
